proof.claim:
Desired state must fail CLOSED: the control plane may only be pointed at an
artifact it can actually resolve and install.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The 2026-08-16 incident began with a deploy that reported
success it had not achieved, and every scenario in this suite until now
observed steady state — none drove the deploy path at all. The pipeline that
failed roughly one run in two had zero scenario coverage of its execution.

This drives the operator-facing half of that path: `globular services desired
set`. It is the single command that turns "an artifact exists" into "the
cluster will install it", and it is where a bad value does the most damage,
because everything downstream treats desired state as authority.

THE PROPERTY. A request naming something the repository cannot resolve must be
REFUSED, not accepted-and-retried-forever. An accepted-but-unresolvable
desired state is a rollout that can never finish and never says so: the
controller keeps trying, reconcile keeps failing, and the operator sees a
cluster that is perpetually "converging". That is strictly worse than an error
at the point of the request.

Three cases are exercised, and the refusals matter more than the acceptance —
which is why they are expressed as actions that FAIL the scenario on the wrong
outcome, rather than as assertions about state afterwards. An action that
quietly succeeded where a refusal was required would otherwise leave desired
state pointing at nothing while the scenario reported PASS.

NOT COVERED HERE, and worth stating plainly: the desired-state REGRESSION
floor. On 2026-08-16 a rollback was refused with "desired floor is 1.2.317,
attempted 1.2.316; pass --allow-regression to override (audited)". Exercising
that needs two published versions of one package, and a bundle ships one
version per package — so proving it needs a publish, not just a desired-state
change. See deploy-publish-then-converge for the half that is reachable.
